You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
This looks like mid-2012. The unemployment rate is 8.2%, which fits May 2012. The fed funds rate is 0.15% and the 10-year yield is 1.60%, down about 63bp over 3 months, which matches the May 2012 Treasury rally. Headline CPI is 1.73% year over year, and May 2012 CPI was about 1.7%.

Equities fit as well. US large-cap fell 2.8% over 3 months, consistent with a May 2012 decline, but it is up 4.1% over 1 month, so the month is more likely June 2012 than May. The June 2012 unemployment rate was 8.2%, and the 10-year yield ended June near 1.65%, against about 1.58% at the end of May. The data fit June better, since the 1-month equity return is positive and developed ex-US is up 7%. May 2012 had a large equity decline, so the end of June fits.

Against that, the 1-month return on 20y+ Treasuries is -1.7%, which fits June, when yields rose slightly. The 10-year yield 3 months earlier, at the end of March 2012, was about 2.23%, so a 63bp change would put the latest at 1.60%. That fits end of June (about 1.64%) reasonably well. The 3-month equity return of -2.8% is also consistent with end of March to end of June, since the S&P 500 returned about -2.8% over that span.

The dollar is up 8.6% year over year, which fits mid-2012 after the euro crisis flows.

I estimate June 2012.
